digest.component_or_area: stability program Track I — defect introduction reduction
propositions: Product-logic representation drift and gate-runtime defects dominate introduction-side bug mechanisms (18.3% and 20.8% respectively in 120-bug sample).
Test isolation under ~90-worktree parallelism contributes 15.8% of defects, with shared-mutable-state-across-workers patterns in completion-cache requiring per-isolation-root keying.
Manual representation mirrors lack committed inventory and enforcement, allowing divergence from MCP tool surface and library facade to go undetected.
Subprocess-spawning tests without harness-enforced isolation roots bypass collection-time validation, permitting isolation class defects.
A deterministic, shrink-only mechanism ratchet must run in make lint to prevent unjustified mechanism additions and track exception decisions.
